speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've had a fever and altered mental state for two days. Have you experienced any severe headache, stiff neck, or seizures during this time?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, could you tell me if you have noticed any new tremors, muscle stiffness, or involuntary movements alongside the fever? Also, have you had any recent head trauma or taken any other new medications recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Creatine Kinase (CK), and Serum Toxicology Screen.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to haloperidol use.
